handbook-scribelectern-views-text:
The Lectern has five tabs, switched via the icon buttons in the right-hand sidebar.

Read — Shows all tasks and notes as a scrollable list. Any player can read, pin, and check off tasks, even while another player holds the editor lock.

Task Editor — Full document editing. Add tasks, edit text, pin rows, reorder by drag, and delete rows. Changes autosave as you type. Only one player may edit at a time.

Pinned — Lists all of your pinned tasks across every Lectern, fully editable in place. Completions apply immediately with no undo delay.

Guest Book — A shared log of who has visited this Lectern. Each reader is recorded with the date of their visit, and visitors can leave a short note. Unlike the private History on a Notebook, the Guest Book is public to everyone who opens the Lectern.

Settings — Opens the Scribe Settings panel (same as the gear icon on the Pinned Task HUD).
handbook-scribelectern-hud-text:
Hover a task row in Read or Edit view and click the pin icon to add it to your Pinned Task HUD — an always-on overlay showing your pinned tasks over the game world. Pins are per-player; pinning a task on a shared Lectern only affects your own HUD.

Checking off a task from the HUD starts a 1.5-second undo window. During that window the task text fades as a countdown and unchecking cancels the action entirely. After the window elapses the completion is applied according to your chosen policy (keep pinned, unpin, sink to bottom, or delete the task). These policies also apply to completed tasks in the Lectern.

Press P (rebindable under Controls: Scribe Mod) or click the Pinned header to shrink the HUD. Position and size are configurable in Scribe Settings.
craftinginfo-scribe-getting-started-text:
What is Scribe?
Scribe is a note-taking and task-management mod. Write tasks and notes, pin them to a persistent HUD overlay visible while you play, and keep them either at a fixed Lectern or in a carried Notebook.

Three ways to carry your notes
Lectern — a placed block. Shared and readable by everyone, with an editor lock and a Guestbook.
Notebook — a personal, carried document that travels in your inventory and keeps its own History chronicle.
Clockmaker's Notebook — a Notebook with an added countdown Timer.

Opening a Lectern
Right-click to open in Read view. Shift+right-click to open in Edit view and request the editor lock. A Notebook opens on right-click while held.

The views
Read: scroll, complete, and pin tasks to your HUD.
Task Editor: also add, edit, reorder, and delete rows. On a Lectern, one player edits at a time.
Pinned: all your pins across every Lectern and Notebook, editable in place.
Settings: all Scribe preferences.

Pinned Task HUD
Hover a task in Read or Edit view and click the pin icon. The task appears on your HUD immediately. Check it off from the HUD to start the 1.5-second undo window; let it elapse to apply your completion policy.

Press P (rebindable) or click the ▾ Pinned header to collapse the HUD.

For keyboard shortcuts and text editing mechanics, see Scribe Mod: Editor Reference in the handbook.
craftinginfo-scribe-editor-reference-tex:
The following functionality is available in the Scribe editor — on the Lectern and in the carried Notebook and Clockmaker's Notebook alike.

Row navigation
Tab — move to the next row.
Shift+Tab — move to the previous row.
Enter — insert a new empty task.
Shift+Enter — insert a hard line break within the current row.
Esc — commit and close the Lectern.

Caret movement
Arrow keys — move one character or line.
Alt/Option+Left/Right — skip by whole word.
Cmd+Left/Right (macOS) or Home/End — jump to line start or end.
Ctrl+Left/Right (Windows) — skip by whole word.
Hold Shift with any movement key to extend the selection.

Selection and clipboard
Ctrl/Cmd+A — select all text in the focused field.
Ctrl/Cmd+C — copy. Ctrl/Cmd+X — cut. Ctrl/Cmd+V — paste.
Typing while text is selected replaces the selection.

Empty task behaviour
When you move focus away from a task row (Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Esc, or clicking elsewhere), the row is committed. If the row is empty or whitespace-only it is automatically deleted and focus moves to the row above. An empty row that still has focus is not deleted.

On commit, trailing blank lines and trailing whitespace are trimmed from a non-empty row. Interior line breaks (from Shift+Enter) are preserved.

Adding tasks
New Task button — always at the bottom of the Editor.
Enter — inserts a task directly below the current row. Both create an empty row ready to type into immediately.
item-scribenotebook-desc: A personal notebook. Write tasks and notes anywhere.
item-scribeclockmakernotebook-desc: A notebook with a built-in timer. Set countdowns in real or in-game time.
handbook-scribenotebook-about-text:
The Notebook is a personal, carried version of the Lectern. Right-click while holding it to open your own document of tasks and notes — it travels with you in your inventory, so your list is always at hand, even far from any Lectern.

Unlike a Lectern, a Notebook belongs to whoever carries it: there is no shared editor lock and no Guestbook. It also keeps a private History chronicle, automatically logging notable events (deaths, temporal storms, boss kills) that happen while you carry it.
handbook-scribenotebook-editor-text:
The Notebook uses the same editor as the Lectern, minus the Guestbook. Tabs switch via the right-hand sidebar:

Read — your tasks and notes as a scrollable list; complete and pin from here.
Task Editor — add, edit, reorder, and delete rows. Changes autosave as you type.
Pinned — every task you have pinned to the HUD, editable in place.
History — the auto-logged event chronicle.

For keyboard shortcuts and text-editing mechanics, see Scribe Mod: Editor Reference.
handbook-scribenotebook-history-text:
Every notebook keeps a private History chronicle on its History tab — a newest-first log that fills in automatically as you carry it. Recorded events include when it was Crafted, who First held it, your Deaths, players you Killed, Bosses defeated, and Temporal Storms weathered while it was on you. You can also add your own dated Notes to the chronicle.

History is per-notebook and travels with the item, so each notebook tells the story of its own owner. This is unlike the Lectern's public Guest Book, which logs visitors to a shared block.
handbook-scribenotebook-craft-text: Craft the Notebook on the crafting grid from a leather cover, a parchment page, a feather quill, a metal nails-and-strips buckle, and a bowl of black ink — see the recipe on this page. Once you have a Notebook you can upgrade it into a Clockmaker's Notebook — the upgrade keeps your tasks and History.
handbook-scribeclockmakernotebook-about-: The Clockmaker's Notebook does everything the plain Notebook does — carried tasks, notes, pins, and an auto-logged History — and adds a built-in Timer tab.
handbook-scribeclockmakernotebook-timer-:
Open the Timer tab to set a single countdown with an optional label and a duration in hours, minutes, and seconds. Choose Real time (counts down in real-world seconds) or In-game time (counts down in game-world time, which runs faster). The timer belongs to you, not the notebook — it keeps running while the Clockmaker's Notebook sits in a chest, and its countdown shows on your Pinned Task HUD.

When it reaches zero the HUD timer blinks and its icon rocks back and forth to get your attention. By default the finished timer disappears from the HUD after about 30 seconds; you can also clear it early by clicking the HUD timer or pressing Stop Timer. If you would rather it stay until you acknowledge it, turn off Timer disappears in Scribe Settings — the finished timer then remains on the HUD until you click it or press Stop Timer.
handbook-scribeclockmakernotebook-craft-:
Craft it on the crafting grid from a Notebook, a temporal gear, and a piece of metal parts — see the recipe on this page.

Requires the Tinkerer trait. By default only players of the Clockmaker character class (which grants the Tinkerer trait) can craft it; if the recipe will not complete for you, that is why. A server operator can lift this requirement for everyone by running /worldconfig scribeClockmakerRequiresTrait false and then restarting the world or server.
